evals.prompt: Wire this repository to my local HVE-Core clone at ~/repos/forks/microsoft-hve-core. Do not install the extension.
evals.expected_output: A local .hve-core symlink, dynamically generated VS Code chat locations, local Git exclusion, and validation without marketplace installation.
expectations: Creates a project-root .hve-core symlink resolving to the supplied absolute clone path.
Adds exactly one .hve-core rule to the repository-local path returned by git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude rather than the shared .gitignore.
Configures agents, prompts, instructions, skills, and hooks through project-relative .hve-core paths.
Each chat.*Locations value is a JSON object mapping paths to boolean true, not an array.
Excludes installer and experimental skill packages by default.
Does not install or modify a marketplace extension.

evals.prompt: Use my local HVE-Core fork for this project. It already has a .vscode/settings.json with Python and editor settings, so preserve those.
evals.expected_output: The existing settings remain intact while HVE-Core chat location maps are merged surgically.
expectations: Preserves unrelated Python, editor, and existing chat location settings.
Adds only missing HVE-Core location entries.
Preserves JSONC comments when the existing file uses JSONC.
Keeps every chat.*Locations setting as an object map from path to boolean true.
Every newly enabled path exists as a directory.

evals.prompt: Set up local HVE-Core here. There is already a real .hve-core directory from an older experiment.
evals.expected_output: The collision is surfaced and no existing directory is replaced without explicit approval.
expectations: Detects that .hve-core is an existing directory rather than the requested symlink.
Stops before deleting, moving, or replacing the directory.
Requests an explicit collision disposition from the user or reports that approval is required when non-interactive.
Leaves .hve-core contents, VS Code settings, Git excludes, and unrelated worktree state unchanged.

evals.prompt: Link this project to my local HVE-Core clone and include the experimental agents and skills too.
evals.expected_output: The normal local wiring includes experimental component directories because the user explicitly opted in.
expectations: Creates a project-root .hve-core symlink resolving to the supplied local clone.
Includes experimental locations for every artifact type where that directory exists.
Includes an experimental subagents directory when present.
Still excludes the installer skill package.
Every configured experimental path exists as a directory.

evals.prompt: Set up local HVE-Core here. A regular file named .hve-core already exists and contains data I need.
evals.expected_output: The regular-file collision is reported and setup stops without mutating the project.
expectations: Detects that .hve-core is a regular file.
Stops before deleting, moving, replacing, or writing inside .hve-core.
Requests an explicit collision disposition from the user or reports that approval is required when non-interactive.
Leaves the file bytes, VS Code settings, Git excludes, and unrelated worktree state unchanged.

evals.prompt: Wire this project to ~/repos/forks/microsoft-hve-core. The existing .hve-core symlink points to a different checkout.
evals.expected_output: The mismatched symlink and both targets are reported, and setup stops without replacing the link.
expectations: Detects that .hve-core resolves to a different target than the requested clone.
Reports both the existing and requested targets.
Stops before unlinking or replacing the symlink.
Leaves the symlink, alternate target, VS Code settings, Git excludes, and unrelated worktree state unchanged.

evals.prompt: Wire this linked Git worktree to my local HVE-Core clone, then verify that running the same setup again makes no changes.
evals.expected_output: The worktree uses the repository-local exclude returned by git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude and a second run is idempotent.
expectations: Creates or reuses a project-root .hve-core symlink resolving to the supplied clone.
Writes exactly one .hve-core rule to the path returned by git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude.
Preserves unrelated exclude rules even when the original file lacks a trailing newline.
Uses git check-ignore -v --no-index to validate local rule attribution.
A second run leaves symlink metadata, settings bytes, exclude bytes, Git status, source state, and extension state unchanged.

evals.prompt: Wire this project to local HVE-Core, but ~/repos/forks/microsoft-hve-core does not exist yet.
evals.expected_output: Setup stops and the user is offered help cloning the official repository into the default local path.
expectations: Expands the default path relative to the current user's home directory.
Stops before creating .hve-core, VS Code settings, or Git exclude entries.
Offers to work with the user to clone https://github.com/microsoft/hve-core.git into ~/repos/forks/microsoft-hve-core.
Does not silently clone or choose a different destination.
